title: Read the recovered flag the right way round and pre-register exposure
hypothesis: The weekly provider segment and the shipped-record acceptance table both rested on a misread field: a `provider_error` incident carrying `final: true` counted as user-visible, while `final` was set when a usable answer closed the retry run. A second defect let a metric filter on the report bucket, which a trace span overwrites, so the qoder catalog baseline read 0.00 while eleven user-visible failures existed.
measurement: Same 28-day harvest as round 7: 715 sessions, 1,678 incidents, 4,178 user turns before the 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z switch. Provider table and weekly segment now share one predicate and one test.
result: The flag is renamed to `recovered` (true = a later usable answer closed the run) and both readers use it; openai-codex before the switch is 3.8 user-visible failures per 100 turns (104 events), not 19.8 (539, which were the recovered ones). Provider detail now keeps the provider's own `code` next to the trace bucket, so qoder catalog failures are countable: 11 user-visible events, baseline 0.263 per 100. Each acceptance record now declares the exposure where its baseline predicts ten events, and the parser refuses any other value.
